Synopsis:
The player discovers an altar in the temple of Shar. They can choose to pray at it, with the chance to receive a buff or debuff depending on the outcome of a religion check. Shar and Selune tags automatically get buff and debuff respectively. Avatar Shadowheart gets a unique and ambigous outcome, casting some doubt on her standing with her goddess.

Cluster Contexts:
- SHA_AcademyAltar.json: The player has found an altar to Shar in a temple and can choose to pray there; the result uses a religion check that can grant a buff or inflict a debuff. Prayers marked Shar or Selûne automatically give the corresponding benefit or penalty, but Shadowheart’s personal outcome is presented as a unique, ambiguous result that can cast doubt on her standing with her goddess. Shadowheart is established (or soon revealed) as a follower of Shar and will react with contempt for Selûne’s iconography; if her faith hasn’t been exposed yet, her praise or sarcasm will be more guarded. Off‑screen context that informs tone includes recent discoveries and tensions—frescoes linking Shar and Selûne, a telepathic assault and Shadowheart’s infernal box, freed allies or wounded fugitives (Halsin, Karlach), or recent combat/stealth—which help explain why remarks at the altar may read as pointed, defensive, or revealing. The sample lines showing Shadowheart calling the shrine “noble” can therefore be read either as a frank devotion or a veiled provocation depending on what the player already knows.
- SHA_Disc_Altar.json: The player is standing before an altar to Shar inside her temple, where a disembodied Voice of Shar monitors their progress and offers modular commentary on the trials and rituals observed so far. The party has already advanced through earlier challenges and reached the inner-threshold; the voice now frames a deliberate choice—stepping into a pool of water to begin the final test to enter the sanctum. Shadowheart (a companion) notes that nothing further can be done until the trials are completed. An inscription and the voice suggest the trials emphasize stealth, martial skill, and devotion (and even hint at a Selûnite blood sacrifice), and the player may or may not recall that Dark Justiciars are Shar’s elite inner circle.
- FOR_Owlbear_OM_Shadowheart_COM.json: Shadowheart reacts to taking offerings made at a shrine to Selûne, the rival of her goddess Shar. If Shadowheart is the avatar, she has a moment of introspection where she considers if she should take the items of not. If Shadowheart is a companion, she encourages the player to not take the items. The player can try talk her around, and may discover she is a Shar worshipper if they don't already know. The outcome of this dialogue potentially strengthens or damages Shadowheart's opinion of the player.
- FOR_SeluneStash_PAD_NoticeShrine.json: The party has come across a small grotto shrine — a statue with prayers and offerings — and are remarking on it. The statue can reasonably be identified as Selûne: Shadowheart and any party member flagged as a cleric or paladin will always recognise her, while others’ responses will reflect their own faith (for example, a Shar-worshipper might sneer, a Selûne-devotee will be reverent, or a pragmatic party member merely points it out). The offerings imply recent local worship activity, but no other on-screen NPCs are required for these lines. Off-screen, the encounter may be happening near other threats (for example, nearby goblin patrols from the ambush cluster), and prior stealth/perception checks could mean enemies are closing in or already watching, which can change the tone of the exchange.
- GOB_ShadowHeart_VB_Temple.json: The party is exploring a goblin-occupied ruin that was once a temple of Selûne; Shadowheart reacts with visible disgust at the desecration and even says the goblins’ crude decorations are an improvement over the surviving Selûne icons. Off-screen context: Selûne and Shar are opposed deities in the setting, and earlier lore (e.g., a fresco or other discoveries) can have already linked the site to that moonrise/Shar conflict. Shadowheart’s lines read as contempt for Selûne’s worship and will sound more pointed if the player already suspects or knows she follows Shar; if her faith is still secret, her barbs are more veiled. The party may also have other recent developments nearby (a wounded Karlach, a freed druid like Halsin, or a telepathic vision and Shadowheart’s infernal box) that explain heightened tension or make a Shar admission more or less likely in the scene.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):

- Shadowheart: Such a noble shrine. I fail to understand why some speak ill of Shar. She radiates grace. (node 19)
